reasoning_details.text:
Now I need to merge the two parent implementations, preserving the small-path logic from the r8-s-pf256-disp version (with its two-tier token thresholds and prefetch/eviction policy handling) exactly as written, while keeping the createpolicy-based eviction approach distinct from the constant-based approach used in the l2mode parent.

For medium and large sizes, I'm pulling in the l2mode logic: 256 threads for mid-range tokens with default weight loading and constant eviction policy, then switching to 512 threads for large token counts when row count is divisible by 32, otherwise falling back to 256. Since all large-token workloads end up with an even token count, the row divisibility condition always holds, simplifying things.

I'm structuring this as a single kernel file with a small-path template and a medium/large template parameterized by thread count and load modes, using launch bounds tuned per thread configuration, and I'll run the compile and test steps together to conserve my limited GPU call budget.
